specPoints.text: understand how division of a diploid cell by mitosis produces two cells that contain identical sets of chromosomes
understand that mitosis occurs during growth, repair, cloning and asexual reproduction

primer.text: Growth, healing, renewal and cloning all lean on one mechanism. This note defines mitosis as the division that yields two genetically identical cells, walks the chromosome-doubling sequence that keeps every daughter diploid, and then maps the four contexts — growth, repair, replacement and asexual reproduction — where the body runs it.

lessons.title: The Cloning Division
lessons.opening: Mitosis is nuclear division that clones: each chromosome copies itself first, the copies line up and are pulled apart, and one original diploid cell becomes two new cells holding identical chromosome sets.
keyPoints: Mitosis gives two cells with identical sets of chromosomes.
Chromosomes duplicate before the division, forming the familiar X shapes.
Copies align at the cell centre and fibres pull them to opposite ends.
The division serves growth, tissue repair, cell replacement and asexual reproduction.

low.restatement: The cell duplicates its chromosomes, splits once, and two matching cells walk away.
low.analogy: A document photocopied once: two pages, same text.
low.examPointer: Name the products as genetically identical, diploid cells.

medium.restatement: Pre-division duplication is what preserves the diploid count in both daughters.
medium.analogy: Copy your shopping list before splitting it, and both halves stay complete.
medium.examPointer: Tie the X shapes to duplication; examiners ask what they are.

check.stem: What does one mitotic division produce?

options.text: Two cells with identical chromosome sets
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.
Four varied products belong to meiosis.
Division halves, it does not enlarge.
The diploid set is preserved.

check.stem: What happens to chromosomes just before mitosis?

options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.
Shrinkage is not part of the sequence.
The chromosomes are the whole point.
Gene swapping is not part of mitosis.

check.stem: During mitosis, what are the X-shaped structures seen in the cell?

options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.
The X shape is normal duplication, not mutation.
Membranes do not form X shapes.
Nuclei re-form after the division.

check.stem: Why does each daughter cell end up diploid?

options.text: Duplication before division keeps two copies of every chromosome in each new cell
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.

options.text: The cell borrows chromosomes from neighbours
options.explanation: Nothing is borrowed.
Duplication happens before the split.
Fertilisation is for gametes, not body cells.

options.text: Duplicate, line up, pull apart, divide
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.
Halving and fusing belong elsewhere.
Duplication precedes division.
Fusing describes fertilisation.

check.modelAnswer: Mitosis is nuclear division that gives rise to genetically identical cells.

check.stem: List the uses of mitosis in the body.
check.modelAnswer: Growth, repair of damaged tissue, replacement of cells, and asexual reproduction.

check.stem: Explain why identical chromosome sets make mitosis suitable for repair.
check.modelAnswer: Replacement tissue must match the original cells, and identical chromosome sets preserve that genetic identity, so the rebuilt tissue works like the tissue it replaces.

check.stem: A lizard regrows its lost tail. State the division involved and what must be true of the new tail cells' chromosomes.
check.modelAnswer: Mitosis rebuilds the tail, and the new cells must carry identical chromosome sets matching the original diploid cells.

lessons.title: Where the Body Runs Mitosis
lessons.opening: Every cell in the body outside the gametes descends from the zygote through mitosis, which is why one mechanism covers growth, the daily replacement of skin and blood cells, and the cloning behind asexual reproduction.
keyPoints: All body cells except gametes arise from mitosis of the zygote.
Growth needs new cells, which mitosis supplies.
Repair replaces damaged or dead cells by the same route.
Asexual reproduction uses mitosis to make offspring identical to the parent.
Skin cells and red blood cells are constantly renewed this way.

low.restatement: Everything but the sex cells comes from mitosis, and it keeps running to renew worn tissue.
low.analogy: One printing press built the whole book and keeps reprinting worn pages.
low.examPointer: Name all four contexts: growth, repair, cloning, asexual reproduction.

medium.restatement: The zygote-to-embryo story shows why identical copies suit development, and renewal shows why the process never stops.
medium.analogy: A city built from one brick mould, with the same mould repairing it forever.
medium.examPointer: Attach concrete examples: skin and red blood cells for renewal.

check.stem: Which cells of the body are not produced by mitosis from the zygote?

options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.
Skin cells renew through mitosis.
Their precursors divide by mitosis.
They derive from mitotic division during development.

check.stem: What does asexual reproduction have in common with wound healing?

options.text: Both rely on mitosis to produce new cells
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.
Meiosis makes gametes, not new tissue or clones.
Neither requires gamete fusion.
Mitosis preserves the diploid set.

check.stem: Why must red blood cells be replaced continually?

options.text: They wear out, and mitosis supplies their replacements
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.
Wear and loss, not mutation, drive renewal.
Blood cells never become sex cells.
Replacement balances loss, not endless doubling.

check.stem: A zygote divides into an embryo. Which process is at work and why?

options.text: Mitosis, because the embryo needs identical copies for growth
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.
Embryo building needs identity, not variation.

options.text: Fertilisation, because the egg must be fertilised again
options.explanation: Fertilisation already happened.
Change here comes from controlled division.

check.stem: Which statement matches the taught account of cloning?

options.text: Mitosis produces offspring genetically identical to the parent
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.
Mixing two parents is sexual reproduction.
Mitosis keeps the diploid set.
Asexual reproduction by mitosis needs none.

check.stem: Name the four contexts in which mitosis occurs.
check.modelAnswer: Growth, repair, cloning and asexual reproduction.

check.stem: State the origin of all body cells apart from gametes.
check.modelAnswer: They are produced by mitosis of the zygote.

check.stem: Explain why a lost skin patch is restored with matching skin rather than a different tissue.
check.modelAnswer: Mitosis copies the surrounding skin cells exactly, so the new cells carry the same chromosomes and mature into the same tissue type.

check.stem: A gardener grows a whole strawberry plant from one cutting without any flowers or seeds. Name the reproduction type and the division that built the new roots and shoots.
check.modelAnswer: It is asexual reproduction, and mitosis produced every new root and shoot cell, keeping the offspring genetically identical to the parent.

glossary.definition: Nuclear division producing two cells with identical chromosome sets.
Carrying two copies of each chromosome, as body cells do.
Reproduction without gamete fusion, yielding offspring identical to the parent.
The fertilised egg from which mitosis builds every body cell.
